title: Greek Salad
description:
Grandma Jackson used to make this for us on special occasions when we’d visit in Florida. Her recipe was from the famous Greek restau-rant in Tarpon Springs – Pappas’.
We always enjoyed this, but it was dramatically different from the Greek salads that we had in Greece (only tomatoes, cucumbers, sliced peppers, onions, olive oil, feta cheese and dried oregano).
Our favorite way of making Greek Salad is a little bit of both!
START TO FINISH: 20 MIN
Greek Salad
Bring water (with a little salt) to boil in saucepan.
Peel the potatoes, if desired, and cut into small bit-sized pieces.
Boil potatoes until tender but still firm, 7-10 minutes. Drain and mix with the mayonnaise, oregano, chopped onion, and salt and pepper to taste.
Meanwhile, prepare the dressing. In a little electric mixer (or by hand), mix well together the garlic, oregano, vinegar, lemon juice, olive oil, and salt and pepper.
When ready to serve, toss the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and scallions with the dressing (you may have a little left over).
Divide the potato salad among the four plates and put portions of the salad on top (hiding the potatoes!).
Sprinkle the salads with crumbled feta.
If desired, garnish with fresh chopped parsley, oregano, or even mint.
Other Items to Add (a la Pappas’)
ingredients: Anchovy slices (or could be mixed in well with the salad dressing)
An avocado, peeled, seeded, and sliced
Green, red, yellow, or orange peppers, julienned or cut into thin rings
For a true “Grecian Salad” (Horiatiki Salata) as opposed to this “Greek Salad”
directions: Combine bite-sized pieces of the cucumbers, tomatoes, peppers, olives, and onions with the olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Then sprinkle on some crumbled feta.
Sometimes, for larger gatherings, with each person having their own special likes or dislikes, Grandma would put all the ingredients out on the counter (a deconstructionist!).
Then, we each could make the salad exactly the way we thought best.
